newsitem.title: UK: European veg oils end mostly higher, thin - Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: European veg oils end mostly higher, thin - Oct 10.

text.p: Closing European vegetable oil prices on Thursday were mostly higher with palm oil underpinned by news earlier which could see Pakistan back in the market.
The State-run Ghee Corporation of Pakistan (GCP) said on Thursday it was negotiating for a $5.0 million financing facility with the Jeddah-based Islamic Development Bank to import vegetable oils.

Rumours on the Malaysian market that Pakistan had already secured as much as $10 million to buy 20,000-30,000 tonnes of vegetable oil were denied by a GCP offical who said they could have been started by speculators trying to move palm oil.

Far East traders estimate that Pakistan could buy between 10,000 to 11,000 tonnes of palm oil if the deal is confirmed, but against forecasts of end-September Malaysian stocks of around 905,000 tonnes this would be a "drop in the ocean", European traders said.
However, trade was generally quiet ahead of the release on Friday of the USDA crop report.
At the close of business crude palm oil was unchanged to $7.50 up while refined palm oil was $2.50 to $5 higher with no futher business reported during the afternoon.
Coconut oil attracted some dealer trading with Sep/Oct fetching $740 and Dec/Jan and Jan/Feb $720 a tonne cif.
Closing sellers were unchanged to $2.50 up while palmkernel oil was unchanged.
Soft oils closed slightly higher depsite the lower Chicago opening with soy oil 0.75 to one guilders up after Nov/Jan traded at 93 and Feb/Apr at 95 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
Dutch/EU rape oil finished 0.50 guilders up to unchanged on a tradeless market.
